newsitem.title: UK: Enviromed says in talks on more disposals.
newsitem.headline: Enviromed says in talks on more disposals.

text.p: The new board of the struggling British healthcare group Enviromed Plc said on Thursday that it was in talks on a series of further disposals.

In a statement to the group's annual shareholder meeting, chairman Ron Zwanziger, who took over following a revolt by shareholders in January, said the new management had decided to sell loss-making businesses in the diagnostics and healthcare divisions.
He said the company was also "in the final stages" of disposing of the heavy metal sensor business, while talks on selling the Epsom day surgery unit were "well underway."
On Tuesday, the group announced the sale of its Euro Laboratories Ltd unit for 135,000 stg.

Zwanziger led a coup against Enviromed's former management, after profits collapsed and the value of the company crumbled from around 112 pence in December 1994 to below 30 pence. However, shares in the group have continued to retreat, touching a low of just 15 pence at the start of April.
The shares fell another two pence to 18 pence in late morning trading on Thursday.
Zwanziger told shareholders that the majority of the group's trading activities were continuing to incur "substantial losses," with the exception of the Biozyme operation in Wales.
